2027-01-05.title: First Tuesday of Denha · Eve of Denha
2027-01-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Strive to enter through the narrow door
2027-01-05.alt: Season of Denha. Tonight many families keep the Denha customs: lamps on plantain stems (pindikuthi) and the night bath recalling the Jordan (rakkuli).
2027-01-05.verse: Strive to enter through the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
theo: On the eve of Denha St Paul gives Titus a short rule for the baptised. Just before today's passage he has spoken of “the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit”; now he adds: “The saying is sure. I desire that you insist on these things, so that those who have come to believe in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works”. Baptism is not a certificate to be filed away; it is a new life to be lived in deeds. Paul also warns against the opposite: “stupid controversies, genealogies, dissensions, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and worthless.” A Christian community can waste its strength in endless arguments while the poor wait at the door.

In the Gospel someone asks Jesus: “Lord, will only a few be saved?” Jesus does not feed curiosity; he speaks to the heart: “Strive to enter through the narrow door”. To have eaten and drunk in his presence is not enough; what counts is a life he can recognise as his own. Yet the door is not narrow because God is mean. The same Gospel promises that “people will come from east and west, from north and south, and will eat in the kingdom of God.” Tomorrow, at the Jordan, Jesus himself goes down into the water and opens the door. Our ancestors kept this night with lights on plantain stems, crying El Paiya, God is light, and with a bath in river or pond recalling the Jordan. Tonight let us ask for the grace to enter by the door he opens.
outline: Ask: what do the lamps and the night bath of the Denha eve mean?
Strive to enter; guests come from east and west.
“Strive to enter through the narrow door.”
live: Light a lamp at home tonight and pray: Christ, light of the world, shine on our family.
A good work instead of an argument (Titus 3:8–9)
Leave aside one useless dispute and do one concrete good work instead.
2027-01-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, tomorrow you go down into the Jordan to open for us the door of life. Keep me from empty quarrels, make me eager for good works, and give me strength to enter through the narrow door into the feast of your kingdom. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is a foretaste of the banquet where people from east and west, north and south eat in the kingdom of God (Luke 13:29). We enter it through the door of Baptism.

quick: Those who believe must devote themselves to good works.
Quarrels and empty controversies are unprofitable and worthless.
Strive to enter through the narrow door; the kingdom is open to all nations.
2027-01-05.action: Light a lamp at home tonight and do one good work before you sleep.
2027-01-05.question: Do I spend more energy on arguments than on good works?

family.explain: Jesus said: try hard to go in through the narrow door. People will come from everywhere, east and west, north and south, to eat at God's great feast. Tomorrow we celebrate Jesus' Baptism, which opens that door for us.
family.intention: We pray that our family may do good works together.
family.ask: Ask: “What good work can we do together this week?”

illus: In a village near Pala, an old man still plants a plantain stem in his courtyard each Denha eve and sets small lamps on it. His grandchildren, home from Bengaluru and Dubai, gather round as he calls out “El Paiya!” He says: I cannot preach, but I can light a lamp and tell them who the Light is.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this eve of your manifestation, open our hearts to your word and lead us through the narrow door. Amen.
share: Those who believe in God must be careful to devote themselves to good works (Titus 3:8). What good work is God asking of me now?
Avoid controversies and quarrels (Titus 3:9). Which argument should I let go of?
Strive to enter through the narrow door (Luke 13:24). What makes the door narrow for me?
pm.resp: Christ our light, lead us in.
interc: For the Church, that she may be known by her good works.
For families keeping the Denha eve, that their lamps may be signs of faith.
For communities divided by quarrels, that they may find peace.
For our group, that we may strive to enter the kingdom together.
pm.close: Father, tomorrow your Son is revealed at the Jordan. Make us zealous for good works, free us from useless quarrels, and bring us from east and west to the table of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, tonight is the eve of Denha. St Paul gives Titus a rule for the baptised: those who have come to believe in God must be careful to devote themselves to good works; these things are excellent and profitable to everyone (Titus 3:8). The faith we received in Baptism is meant to be seen in our hands.

Paul also warns against what drains a community's strength: stupid controversies, genealogies, dissensions and quarrels, which are unprofitable and worthless (Titus 3:9). How many families and parishes lose years in such arguments, while the poor wait at the door.

In the Gospel someone asks Jesus: Lord, will only a few be saved? Jesus gives no number. He says: strive to enter through the narrow door (Luke 13:23–24). It is not enough to say, we ate and drank with you. The Lord looks for a life he can recognise. And yet he promises that people will come from east and west, from north and south, and will eat in the kingdom of God (Luke 13:29).

Tomorrow Jesus goes down into the Jordan, and the door of heaven opens. Our ancestors kept this night with lamps on plantain stems, crying El Paiya, God is light, and with a bath that recalled the Jordan. Let us light a lamp in our hearts tonight, put aside one quarrel and do one good work, so that we may enter by the door he opens. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight is the eve of Denha! In many homes people light lamps and say: God is light! Light a lamp with your family, and do one good thing for someone before you go to sleep.

intro: Theme: “Strive to enter through the narrow door.”
Good works, not quarrels; the narrow door opened at the Jordan.

q: learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.

The saying is sure. I desire that you insist on these things, so that those who have come to believe in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works; these things are excellent and profitable to everyone.
points.apply: Do one concrete good work for a neighbour this week.

sub: Unity is a work of faith.
q: The beginning of strife is like letting out water; so stop before the quarrel breaks out.
But avoid stupid controversies, genealogies, dissensions, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and worthless.
points.apply: Let go of one argument you keep returning to.

sub: Will only a few be saved?
From east and west to the feast.
q: This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it.
Strive to enter through the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
points.apply: Light a lamp tonight and pray for all who seek the door of faith.

concl: Tomorrow Christ goes down into the Jordan and the door of heaven opens.
Let us enter with lamps lit and hands full of good works.
2027-01-05.resolve: Keep the Denha eve with a lamp, family prayer and one good work.
